content: In this paper, we introduce Dolores, a new paradigm of learning knowledge graph embeddings where we learn not only contextual independent embeddings of entities and relations but also multiple context-dependent embeddings each capturing a different layer of abstraction. We demonstrate that by leveraging connections between three seemingly distinct fields namely: (a) large-scale network analysis, (b) natural language processing and (c) knowledge graphs we are able to learn rich knowledge graph embeddings that are deep and contextualized in contrast to prior models that are typically shallow. Moreover, our learned embeddings can be easily incorporated into existing knowledge graph prediction models to improve their performance. Specifically, we show that our embeddings are not only a “drop-in” replacement for existing models that use embedding layers but also significantly improve the state-of-the-art models on a variety of tasks, sometimes by almost $9.5\%$ . Furthermore, our method is inherently online and scales to large data-sets.
